gen-mystery-quest-gf-sofia-sans-condense: Mystery Quest has open jaws on its curves. Sofia Sans Condensed sits below it in a sans with no thick-thin shading, tall and compact, so paragraphs move along briskly.
gen-mystery-quest-gf-spline-sans-mono: Spline Sans Mono types out every letter at a fixed width, with lowercase nearly as tall as its capitals. And Mystery Quest, with its open curves and low stroke variation, gives that precision a bookish, nostalgic counterweight.
gen-mystery-quest-gf-strait: Soft, nostalgic, a bit storybook. Strait follows in a sans with big round lowercase bowls, so a long passage feels friendly and modern beneath Mystery Quest's open-jawed curves.
gen-mystery-quest-gf-tiny5: Mystery Quest leaves its curves open at the jaws. Tiny5 is a sans-serif whose ascenders look short because the letters stand so tall, which makes a long passage feel compact and tidy.
gen-mystery-quest-gf-truculenta: Truculenta packs short ascenders and a tall x-height into a compact line, yet its rounded forms stay open. And Mystery Quest earns its keep big and short, where its open curves and bookish tone get room.
gen-mystery-quest-gf-viga: Open-jawed curves give Mystery Quest its storybook look. Viga, a plain sans with no hairlines or shadows, and capitals barely taller than its lowercase, gives those quirks a quiet, uniform floor to stand on.
gen-mystery-quest-gf-voces: Nostalgic and a little bookish up top. But Voces holds its own with tall lowercase and stems close to its hairlines, a sans where change in weight is present yet never dramatic.
gen-mystery-quest-gf-winky-rough: Winky Rough keeps its lowercase nearly as tall as its capitals. Mystery Quest does its best work with open-jawed curves and bookish charm, while this plain sans simply carries the text.
gen-mystery-quest-gf-winky-sans: Nostalgic is the first word that comes to mind for Mystery Quest, with its open curves. Winky Sans follows in a modern sans whose capitals barely rise above the lowercase, so a long passage reads smoothly.
